events.did: twisted the jagged half of the glass shard still wrapped in his hand, driving it deeper into Victor's side
events.quote_anchor: Eli’s hand was still wrapped around the other half. He twisted the jagged piece, and Victor groaned, his heightened nerves turning the ache to agony.

events.did: counted the shots he had fired and found that only one bullet was left, which he was saving
events.quote_anchor: Which was how he knew, he only had one bullet left.

events.did: let go of the glass and stepped back, his hands healing rapidly but with thick white scars roped around the palms
events.quote_anchor: Eli felt the change as well, and let go of the glass, stepping back as if to admire his work.

events.did: dragged the first shard of glass out of his side and pried the second from his shoulder, then flung the first away
events.quote_anchor: “Déjà vu,” said Victor as he dragged the first shard of glass out of his side and flung it away. He pried the second from his shoulder.

events.did: crossed to the knife on the floor, made his way to Victor, and lifted the blade to cut his throat
events.quote_anchor: Deeming it worthy of the task, he made his way to Victor. “I’ll see you on the other side,” he said, the blade catching the light as he lifted it

events.did: entered the room from the doorway and ordered Eli to give him the knife, but never got the last word out
events.quote_anchor: “Give me the knife,” said Gabriel, taking a step into the room. “I’ll finish this mysel—”

events.did: grabbed Eli's body and pulled him down out of the way, then swung the gun up and fired his last shot into Gabriel's head
events.quote_anchor: so he’d have a clear line when he swung the gun up and fired his last shot into Gabriel’s head.

events.did: collapsed inward on himself and turned to ash after Gabriel died, leaving only the small blood-crusted blade
events.quote_anchor: One second, he was there, knife slicing toward Victor’s throat, and the next, his body was collapsing inward on itself.

relations.did: tried to share his pain with Eli, but it did not seem to be enough
relations.quote_anchor: He tried to share the pain, make Eli feel what he did. But for once, it didn’t seem to be enough.

relations.did: held Eli in place by command so his body was pinned when he appeared in the doorway
relations.quote_anchor: Eli froze, the knife halfway to Victor’s throat, his body pinned by Gabriel’s command.

relations.did: shared a current of energy with every resurrected body, a signature that was his but not theirs, including Eli's
relations.quote_anchor: That, combined with the fact that every resurrected body possessed the same current of energy. A signature that wasn’t theirs, but Gabriel’s.

relations.did: had been fairly sure Gabriel would intercede but was far less certain about the link between their lives and deaths
relations.quote_anchor: Victor had been fairly sure Gabriel would intercede, but as for the link between their lives—and deaths—he had been far less certain.

numbers.quote_anchor: If someone had asked him how sure he’d been that Gabriel would come, he’d have said 85 percent.

numbers.did: the eleven self-help books his parents had cowritten
numbers.quote_anchor: He owed that to Alan and Martha Vale, to the eleven self-help books his parents had cowritten.
